questions.learningObjective: Distinguish per-instance NAT from load balancing
questions.stem: An administrator connects to the CLZ-230 frontend on TCP 50001. How is the target selected?

options.A: The health probe alternates RDP sessions across both VMs
options.B: The client selects a VM by putting its name in the password
options.C: The NAT rule association directs that port to the first backend NIC
options.D: The outbound rule chooses whichever VM has lower CPU

optionExplanations.A: A per-instance NAT mapping is not a load-balancing rule.
optionExplanations.B: The password authenticates the guest and does not select a NIC.
optionExplanations.C: This specific rule references web[0], so it targets one VM.
optionExplanations.D: Outbound SNAT does not distribute inbound RDP.

questions.stem: Which frontend-to-backend port mapping is declared by CLZ-230's rdp_first rule?

options.A: TCP 3389 to TCP 50001
options.B: TCP 50001 to TCP 3389
options.C: TCP 80 to UDP 3389
options.D: UDP 50001 to TCP 443

optionExplanations.A: This reverses the declared direction.
optionExplanations.B: The public administration port is forwarded to the guest RDP port.
optionExplanations.C: HTTP distribution and the TCP RDP NAT mapping are different rules.
optionExplanations.D: The rule uses TCP and targets RDP, not browser HTTPS.

questions.stem: Which address should a learner enter for the lesson's external RDP NAT test?

options.A: The web subnet address followed by port 80
options.B: The second VM's private IP from an ordinary Internet laptop
options.C: The resource-group name followed by port 443
options.D: The load balancer public IP with frontend port 50001

optionExplanations.A: A subnet prefix is not a remote host endpoint.
optionExplanations.B: That private address is not directly Internet-routable.
optionExplanations.C: A resource-group name is not the load balancer endpoint.
optionExplanations.D: The NAT frontend is the externally reachable entry point.

questions.learningObjective: Match NSG rules to translated traffic
questions.stem: Why does CLZ-230's workload NSG permit destination port 3389 rather than 50001 for the RDP path?

options.A: NSGs can filter only Windows default ports
options.B: The backend sees the translated guest RDP destination port
options.C: The public frontend listens on 3389 in this implementation
options.D: The health probe rewrites all destination ports

optionExplanations.A: NSGs can filter custom TCP or UDP ports.
optionExplanations.B: Frontend port forwarding maps 50001 to 3389 before delivery to the VM.
optionExplanations.C: The declared frontend port is 50001.
optionExplanations.D: Health probes do not perform NAT for client sessions.

questions.stem: The learner's current public IPv4 is 198.51.100.25 in an illustrative scenario. What prefix length should scope that one address in admin_cidr?

optionExplanations.A: A /24 permits a range of addresses, not only one.
optionExplanations.B: A /16 greatly broadens the permitted source range.
optionExplanations.C: A /0 covers the whole IPv4 address space.
optionExplanations.D: A /32 selects a single IPv4 address; use the learner's actual address in a real lab.

questions.learningObjective: Match the protocol throughout the RDP forwarding path
questions.stem: A learner adds an NSG allow for UDP 3389, but the CLZ-230 TCP NAT connection still fails. Why is that rule insufficient?

options.A: UDP permission automatically opens every TCP port
options.B: The public frontend uses an HTTP proxy for RDP
options.C: The declared NAT mapping and RDP test use TCP, so their TCP path needs permission
options.D: The frontend port must always equal the guest port

optionExplanations.A: TCP and UDP are separate protocols in NSG matching.
optionExplanations.B: This Layer 4 mapping does not provide an HTTP proxy.
optionExplanations.C: Allow the configured TCP destination path while retaining the narrow administrator source.
optionExplanations.D: Port forwarding deliberately maps frontend 50001 to backend 3389; equality is unnecessary.

questions.stem: Which object does azurerm_network_interface_nat_rule_association.rdp_first reference in CLZ-230?

options.A: azurerm_network_interface.web[0]
options.B: Every NIC in the Azure subscription
options.C: Only the AzureBastionSubnet resource
options.D: The public IP's DNS label

optionExplanations.A: The declared association targets the first counted backend NIC.
optionExplanations.B: The relationship specifies a single NIC.
optionExplanations.C: No Bastion subnet is part of this NAT association.
optionExplanations.D: The association uses the private NIC's internal IP configuration.

questions.learningObjective: Avoid assuming all backends have RDP NAT
questions.stem: The implementation creates two Windows VMs but only one inbound NAT association. What can port 50001 reach?

options.A: Both backends in round-robin order
options.B: Only whichever backend currently serves HTTP
options.C: Both backends simultaneously in one RDP session
options.D: Only the first backend, subject to NSG and guest readiness

optionExplanations.A: The rule is not an RDP load-balancing rule.
optionExplanations.B: HTTP flow selection is independent of the NAT mapping.
optionExplanations.C: A client session targets a single mapped VM.
optionExplanations.D: The second VM has no association with this NAT rule.

questions.stem: Does the lesson's per-instance inbound NAT rule need the HTTP health probe to choose its RDP target?

options.A: Yes; the HTTP probe reads the administrator password
options.B: Yes; the probe changes 80 into 3389
options.C: No; the explicit NAT association selects the target without a health probe
options.D: No; because every Windows VM automatically gets a public IP

optionExplanations.A: Probes do not authenticate Windows users.
optionExplanations.B: Probe configuration does not transform service ports.
optionExplanations.C: Inbound NAT mapping does not use a probe to select the designated VM.
optionExplanations.D: These backend NICs are private; explicit NAT supplies access.

questions.stem: Test-NetConnection succeeds against the public IP on 50001. What remains unproven?

options.A: Successful authenticated RDP access to the intended Windows guest
options.B: The existence of any network path to that port
options.C: Whether the local workstation can open any TCP socket
options.D: Whether the frontend port number is present in the command

optionExplanations.A: TCP reachability is narrower than a working authenticated session.
optionExplanations.B: A successful test demonstrates that path at the time of testing.
optionExplanations.C: The test already opened a socket to the target.
optionExplanations.D: The command used that specified port.

questions.stem: CLZ-230 permits admin_cidr at priority 110 and denies other RDP at priority 120. Why does the chosen source remain permitted?

options.A: The highest numerical priority always wins
options.B: The lower-numbered matching allow rule is evaluated first
options.C: A Deny rule is ignored whenever a load balancer exists
options.D: RDP passwords bypass every network rule

optionExplanations.A: Lower priority numbers are evaluated first.
optionExplanations.B: The broad later deny restricts sources that do not match the allow.
optionExplanations.C: NSG policy still applies to backend traffic.
optionExplanations.D: Credentials cannot bypass a blocked network path.

questions.learningObjective: Keep HTTP and RDP roles separate
questions.stem: Which declared rule continues distributing ordinary HTTP traffic while RDP uses its single target?

options.A: The RDP rule's frontend port 50001
options.B: The administrator /32 validation expression
options.C: The load-balancing rule for TCP frontend 80 and backend 80
options.D: The Terraform sensitive password output

optionExplanations.A: That port maps to the Windows RDP service.
optionExplanations.B: Input validation does not distribute traffic.
optionExplanations.C: HTTP uses the backend pool and probe separately from RDP NAT.
optionExplanations.D: An output is not a forwarding rule.

questions.learningObjective: Keep outbound and inbound roles separate
questions.stem: Which CLZ-230 rule supplies backend-initiated Internet egress?

options.A: The per-instance inbound RDP NAT rule
options.B: The explicit load balancer outbound rule
options.C: The deny-other-rdp NSG rule
options.D: The resource group's Project tag

optionExplanations.A: Inbound port forwarding does not supply a general egress design.
optionExplanations.B: The rule declares SNAT for outbound flows from the backend pool.
optionExplanations.C: An inbound deny rule cannot provide egress translation.
optionExplanations.D: Metadata does not implement packet forwarding.

questions.stem: The session opens on the wrong VM after a configuration edit. Which relationship should be inspected?

options.A: The health probe's HTTP page title
options.B: The Terraform binary filename
options.C: The outbound rule's protocol alone
options.D: The NIC-to-inbound-NAT-rule association

optionExplanations.A: The NAT target is not selected by page content.
optionExplanations.B: The filename does not choose the mapped NIC.
optionExplanations.C: Outbound translation is separate from the inbound target.
optionExplanations.D: That relationship identifies the target private IP configuration.

questions.learningObjective: Review a frontend port change completely
questions.stem: A learner changes the NAT frontend port from 50001 to 50002. Which follow-up is needed?

options.A: Update any hard-coded port output and client validation commands to match
options.B: Change the guest RDP service to port 50002 automatically
options.C: Replace the HTTP probe with an RDP username
options.D: Add a public IP to both private NICs

optionExplanations.A: The declared mapping, reported port, and client endpoint must agree.
optionExplanations.B: The backend port can remain 3389; a frontend change does not reconfigure Windows.
optionExplanations.C: Probes do not accept usernames as target ports.
optionExplanations.D: The NAT frontend already provides the intended path.

questions.stem: admin_cidr remains 203.0.113.10/32 while the learner uses a different real public IP. What is the expected risk?

options.A: The source restriction will not permit the learner's actual RDP traffic
options.B: Azure converts that prefix into the current client's address
options.C: The value opens RDP to everyone because /32 is broad
options.D: The value changes the backend RDP port to 2030

optionExplanations.A: Documentation example addresses must be replaced before a real connectivity test.
optionExplanations.B: Azure does not infer the caller's address from an example value.
optionExplanations.C: A /32 is narrow, although this address is only an example.
optionExplanations.D: A source CIDR does not change the destination port.

questions.stem: Which production alternative best removes this lesson's Internet-facing RDP NAT pattern?

options.A: An unscoped Internet allow rule on port 3389
options.B: Publishing the Windows password on the IIS page
options.C: Changing 50001 to another high port without source restrictions
options.D: Bastion or an approved VPN/ExpressRoute-based private management path

optionExplanations.A: That broadens exposure rather than removing it.
optionExplanations.B: A secret on a public page is not a private management path.
optionExplanations.C: A different port is not an access boundary.
optionExplanations.D: These approaches support private administration without the public per-VM NAT exposure.

questions.stem: Which Azure CLI result most directly confirms the intended NAT rule configuration?

options.A: An IIS page containing the resource-group name
options.B: An inbound-nat-rule entry with frontendPort 50001 and backendPort 3389
options.C: An outbound rule with protocol All only
options.D: A VM list that shows two administrator usernames

optionExplanations.A: Page content does not list the NAT rule's configured ports.
optionExplanations.B: Those fields describe the declared mapping.
optionExplanations.C: That confirms egress configuration, not the inbound mapping.
optionExplanations.D: Usernames do not describe load balancer NAT ports.

questions.stem: The NSG source and NAT association are correct, but the guest RDP service is unavailable. What should the learner expect?

options.A: The load balancer automatically installs an RDP service
options.B: HTTP probe health guarantees authenticated RDP works
options.C: Network forwarding alone will not create a usable RDP session
options.D: Changing the Terraform tag removes the need for a listener

optionExplanations.A: The network service does not configure guest services.
optionExplanations.B: HTTP port health does not prove RDP readiness.
optionExplanations.C: The guest must listen and permit the session as well.
optionExplanations.D: Tags do not start the service.

questions.stem: Why do the backend Windows NICs not need their own public IPs for this demonstration?

options.A: The guest password includes an embedded public route
options.B: The load balancer frontend forwards the mapped port to a private backend
options.C: Azure makes every private IP Internet-routable
options.D: An A record automatically creates public NIC addresses

optionExplanations.A: Passwords do not establish routes.
optionExplanations.B: The public endpoint is supplied by the shared frontend.
optionExplanations.C: Private IPs remain private.
optionExplanations.D: DNS records do not allocate public IP resources.

questions.stem: If all inbound NSG allows are removed from the private backends, what happens to the NAT path?

options.A: The NAT declaration alone does not grant permitted backend traffic
options.B: Every frontend port becomes permitted by default
options.C: The service switches automatically to Bastion
options.D: Only the Terraform plan becomes encrypted

optionExplanations.A: Standard forwarding still requires an allowed network path.
optionExplanations.B: The NAT rule is not a blanket access grant.
optionExplanations.C: Bastion is a separate deployed service.
optionExplanations.D: Network policy changes do not alter plan encryption.

questions.stem: Which claim about CLZ-230's RDP NAT rule is accurate?

options.A: It validates every Windows password before forwarding TCP
options.B: It reads the RDP desktop pixels to select a backend
options.C: It forwards a selected transport port rather than authenticating the Windows user
options.D: It encrypts Terraform state while the session is active

optionExplanations.A: The Layer 4 service does not perform Windows guest authentication.
optionExplanations.B: Backend association is explicit, not content based.
optionExplanations.C: Guest credentials and access remain Windows responsibilities.
optionExplanations.D: Traffic forwarding does not encrypt local state.

questions.stem: Why should a learner budget for two Windows instances when inspecting CLZ-230's current Terraform?

options.A: Every inbound NAT rule automatically creates two extra VMs
options.B: Port 50001 represents a count of 50,001 servers
options.C: The HTTP probe multiplies the VM count by two
options.D: Both NIC and VM resources have count = 2 despite a single RDP NAT target

optionExplanations.A: Rules do not independently create Windows instances.
optionExplanations.B: A port is not resource cardinality.
optionExplanations.C: Probes do not create backend VMs.
optionExplanations.D: One NAT association does not reduce the number of declared VMs.

questions.learningObjective: Respond to a rejected broad RDP input
questions.stem: Terraform rejects admin_cidr = 0.0.0.0/0. Which correction follows the lesson?

options.A: Supply one real current public IPv4 /32 for the administrator
options.B: Disable validation and keep the universal source range
options.C: Change the same broad range to a Role tag
options.D: Use an administrator password as the CIDR string

optionExplanations.A: The lesson explicitly limits direct RDP to one source.
optionExplanations.B: That removes the intended safety constraint.
optionExplanations.C: Tags do not define the permitted source rule.
optionExplanations.D: A password is not a network prefix.

questions.stem: The NAT lab generates a Windows administrator password. How should its state and saved plan be handled?

options.A: As harmless public files because the output has sensitive = true
options.B: As potentially sensitive artifacts kept out of public Git history
options.C: As safe attachments whenever the NAT port is nonstandard
options.D: As files that must be copied into the IIS web root

optionExplanations.A: Sensitive output redaction does not sanitize state.
optionExplanations.B: Terraform artifacts can retain values associated with guest credentials.
optionExplanations.C: Port selection does not protect stored secrets.
optionExplanations.D: Publishing state can expose credentials and resource details.

questions.learningObjective: Do not mistake port obscurity for authorization
questions.stem: Why is frontend port 50001 alone insufficient security for this lesson's RDP exposure?

options.A: Ports above 49152 automatically enforce Microsoft Entra MFA
options.B: Only the creator can connect to high-numbered Azure ports
options.C: A discoverable port still needs source restrictions and strong authenticated access
options.D: A high port encrypts the Terraform configuration

optionExplanations.A: Port numbers do not enable MFA.
optionExplanations.B: There is no creator-only port authorization.
optionExplanations.C: Changing the port does not establish identity or trust.
optionExplanations.D: Port choice does not encrypt configuration files.

questions.learningObjective: Review changes before deploying NAT exposure
questions.stem: Which step lets the learner inspect a proposed change to the NAT rule before applying it?

options.A: Run terraform plan with the intended inputs and review the saved plan
options.B: Delete the local state file and rely on the frontend
options.C: Run Test-NetConnection against a port not yet deployed
options.D: Change the browser theme to dark

optionExplanations.A: A plan displays the forwarding and policy changes without executing them.
optionExplanations.B: Removing state breaks tracking instead of reviewing changes.
optionExplanations.C: A live probe cannot describe an unapplied Terraform change.
optionExplanations.D: The theme does not inspect infrastructure actions.

questions.stem: Which result completes the lesson's cleanup evidence after the documented destroy?

options.A: The RDP window closes but the VMs remain running
options.B: Port 50001 times out while the public IP is still allocated
options.C: terraform fmt succeeds without changes
options.D: The captured lesson resource-group name returns false from az group exists

optionExplanations.A: Closing a client does not delete resources.
optionExplanations.B: A failed connection does not prove resource removal.
optionExplanations.C: Formatting is unrelated to deletion.
optionExplanations.D: The verification confirms the managed group is absent.

questions.learningObjective: Avoid treating a NAT mapping as high availability
questions.stem: Why is the first backend's RDP mapping not a highly available pooled administration endpoint?

options.A: The outbound rule only supports DNS
options.B: It stays associated with one designated backend and can fail when that VM is unavailable
options.C: The HTTP frontend lacks a public IP
options.D: RDP maps each request through an HTTP URL path

optionExplanations.A: The rule's protocol is All, and it is unrelated to RDP failover.
optionExplanations.B: Per-instance forwarding does not fail over administration to a different guest.
optionExplanations.C: The frontend has a Standard public IP.
optionExplanations.D: RDP is not HTTP path routing.

questions.stem: Which operational addition fits a temporary production NAT exception?

options.A: Time-bounded source access, monitoring, and an assigned owner
options.B: A permanent universal RDP source to avoid IP changes
options.C: A shared password committed with the Terraform plan
options.D: Removing logs so administrators cannot be traced

optionExplanations.A: Temporary exceptions still require accountable access and review.
optionExplanations.B: That expands risk and contradicts source scoping.
optionExplanations.C: Credentials should not be published.
optionExplanations.D: Auditable operations require appropriate records.
